highlights.title: Fast mode and model reasoning settings
changes: A new "Use Fast mode" toggle prefers faster AI responses when available.
Fast mode may cost more and will fall back to standard processing if fast capacity is unavailable.
Each configured food-analysis model now includes a "Reasoning effort" picker to set analysis depth.
Higher reasoning effort can increase response time and cost.
Saved effort choices stay with each model, update from the catalog, and revert to the model default if unsupported.

includedPullRequests.title: Harden image routing validation and deadlines
includedPullRequests.body:
Label extraction previously accepted huge finite nutrient values and near-zero serving counts that could crash integer conversion or inflate serving totals. Classification and label requests also relied on inactivity timeouts, allowing trickling responses to delay the normal fallback indefinitely.

This change resolves the adversarial review findings:

- Bound accepted label nutrients to 0...1000 grams and serving counts to 0.01...10000; invalid results fall back before reaching display or serving calculations.
- Enforce total deadlines of 8 seconds for classification and 20 seconds for label extraction, cancel the transport on timeout or user cancellation, and finish streams at `[DONE]` even if the connection stays open.
- Add an injectable coordinator boundary and behavioral tests for label reuse, actual serving totals, classifier/extractor failures, description handling, refinement, comparison/retry, cancellation, and repeated identical captures.

Validation: reproduced the numeric acceptance failure and both trickling deadline failures before fixing them. The final iOS simulator build/test run passed all 50 AI test functions (52 runs), with zero failures or skips, including real URLSession transport deadline, completion, and cancellation tests. Native UI testing is deferred to local testing on the headless host.

Image routing remains experimental and disabled by default. The Decisions API inline image encoding has not been verified with live OpenRouter inference because this environment has no API key.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Food-image classification and nutrition-label extraction now stop at their deadlines, even when data or keepalives continue, and cancel the underlying connection.
  * A completed label stream closes promptly, and cancelled analysis stops consuming the stream.
  * Nutrition-label results with incomplete, non-finite, or out-of-range values now fall back to general food analysis instead of being displayed or scaled.
* **Tests**
  * Added coverage for deadlines, cancellation, image-routing decisions, and unsafe nutrition values.
